subject: religious-studies
title: One God or Many?
welcome_lead: Explore how religions answer the deepest question: how many gods are there?
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on monotheism and polytheism across world religions.
final_note: You now understand the difference between monotheistic and polytheistic faiths.

concepts.def: Belief in many gods or deities.
Faiths tracing back to Abraham: Judaism, Christianity, Islam.
View that God's existence cannot be known for sure.
A god or goddess worshipped in a religion.

walkthroughs.body_html: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are monotheistic — they teach that there is only one God who created everything. Sikhism also teaches belief in one God, called Waheguru.

Hinduism is often described as polytheistic because Hindus worship many deities such as Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. However, many Hindus believe these gods are all aspects of one ultimate reality called Brahman.
Buddhism is unusual — most Buddhists do not focus on a creator God. Instead they follow the teachings of the Buddha to escape suffering and reach enlightenment (Nirvana).
